Subject: Question: mid-cycle apportionment on invoice 2027-04-01

Hi Connor,

We received invoice invoice_20270401.pdf dated 2027-04-01. Our AP team flagged a billing line that looks like the same streaming workload was billed across two sub-accounts ("prod-app" and "batch-ingest") during the mid-cycle cutover. That resulted in duplicated per-token charges and VAT being applied differently to each line.

High-level:
- Invoice total: EUR 18,320
- Lumina applied payment hold: EUR 2,100 (withheld until we reconcile VAT on the duplicated lines)

Can you help us with:
1) A breakdown showing which request_ids (or at least a short sample) were attributed to each sub-account at the time window 2027-03-29 22:00 to 2027-04-01 02:00 UTC.
2) Clarify how redirection during canary -> prod rollout is attributed to billing (prefix vs request-level attribution).
3) Confirm whether a credit or invoice adjustment is possible for duplicated tokens and whether VAT will be reclassified for the adjusted lines.

I attached the invoice and the AP note (lumina_ap_evidence.pdf). We're trying to clear payment promptly but AP needs the VAT position to release the hold.

Appreciate a quick look — we have month-end close next week.

Thanks,
Evan
Finance Manager
Lumina Labs

Hi all — I pulled the start of the window and ran initial attribution scans. A few technical notes so expectations are clear:

How attribution works (short):
- Primary rule: attribution follows the request-level metadata (customer_id + subaccount tag).
- Fallbacks: in some high-throughput streaming paths we fall back to session/prefix when request metadata is absent for performance reasons.
- During deployments there's a short overlap where traffic can be produced by both old and new routing tables; that overlap can lead to tokens being recorded under two different subaccount tags if a proxy replay occurs.

Preliminary findings for 2027-03-29 22:00 -> 2027-04-01 02:00 UTC:
- We see ~11,340 requests matching pattern `req_*` that were attributed to both prod-app and batch-ingest in separate records. Likely cause: a short replication window where the streaming ingestion client retried on a different endpoint during the rollout.
- Estimated duplicated token count: ~14,500 tokens (this is an initial estimate; raw logs below needed for exact match).

What we need from Lumina AP to finalize:
1) 3–5 sample request IDs from your logs in that exact window (full ID if possible).
2) Confirmation of any internal replay/backup job that might have re-submitted the same payloads during your deployment.

If confirmed as duplication we propose:
- Credit: full token-level credit for duplicated tokens (we will re-issue a credit memo)
- VAT handling: Redwood can zero-rate the duplicated token lines in the adjustment invoice and issue a corrected VAT breakdown; however, final VAT treatment will follow the tax rules for your EU entity — we can provide the documentation needed for your AP.

I'll attach an abbreviated usage CSV (sample) and a request_id dump once Evan provides the 3 samples.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference

Evan — received the samples, thanks. I ran a targeted join against our request-id index. Findings (short):

- Matched duplicates: 3 of 4 sample IDs appear twice in separate attribution records.
- Extrapolated duplicate token count: 14,320 tokens (± 240).

Proposed remediation:
- Issue credit memo: EUR 1,820 (token-credit equivalent for the duplicated tokens) on a corrected invoice. Credit memo will include a revised VAT breakdown that zeroes out VAT on the duplicated token lines.
- Timing: we'll generate the credit memo and corrected invoice by 2027-04-09 EOD PT and provide a DocuSign link for the formal credit memo acknowledgement (if required).
- Payment hold: once you accept the credit memo the AP team can apply the credit and release the EUR 2,100 hold on your outgoing payment; any remaining delta after the credit will be payable per normal terms.

Notes on evidence and audit trail:
- I'll attach the small request_id extract and a CSV of the per-request attribution for your finance team.
- If you require a deeper raw-log export (complete request payloads) we'll need a short Redactions/POA agreement; let us know.

Thanks,
